extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society; natural philosophers and practicing experimentalists (17th-century scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Short observational and experimental reports in natural philosophy (17th-century Royal Society style): describe phenomena, record measurements and dates, give apparatus and methods, compare with prior observations, and recommend further enquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of data before answering a question
rubrics_metrics.description: the data, or circumstances given him, are not sufficient for determining the question, which therefore he declines for the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt definitive solutions when the provided data are inadequate; explicitly note insufficiency and withhold judgement until further information is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend further observations to settle particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: He concludes by recommending farther observations, to settle these particulars more accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where preliminary measurements or inferences are made, urge additional, targeted observations to confirm or refine the proposed values/interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record precise observational dates and circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: I have observed the position of the comet since January 28, every day, when the weather permitted, viz. January 19, February 6, 10, 17, 19, 24, 26, 27, and March 6, 7, 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give exact dates (and note gaps) and record conditions (e.g., 'when the weather permitted') so later readers can assess continuity and reliability of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide quantitative positional/measurable data
rubrics_metrics.description: He finds the said circle inclined to the ecliptic about 36° 30'; ... it declines from the equator about 26°, and cuts it towards the 11°; ... places its perigee, March 27, in about 15° of Pisces...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report measured angles, inclinations, nodes, dates of perigee/conjunction, latitudes/longitudes, and other numerical parameters to allow independent verification and comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare observations with historical records and other observers
rubrics_metrics.description: I have added an observation which I find that Signior Cassini has not made, viz. that there was ground to think, that the comet of 1652 was the same with the present, seeing that, besides the parity of the swiftness of its motion, the perigee of it was also over against the Great Dog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate current observations to past records and to other observers' accounts to assess recurrence, identity of objects, and consistencies or discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-drawn figures as authoritative representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Hook's Micrographia ... many of the figures are a kind of standard representations, from which most succeeding authors on similar subjects have copied. The figures were all drawn by his own hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include carefully prepared figures (preferably drawn by the observer) because clear imagery can become the standard reference for later work; note any known 'minute faults'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed, step-by-step description of experimental and technical procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The manner of getting the mercury is this: They take of the earth, brought up in buckets, and put into a sieve... it is carried to a stream of running water, and washed as long as any thing will pass through the sieve... the fine small earth... is put into iron retorts and stopped... The fire forces the mercury into the receivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe methods and process sequences (tools, sizes, order of operations, times) in sufficient detail that others can reproduce or judge the technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simple empirical indicators as process quality controls
rubrics_metrics.description: They remain twenty-four hours, or until an egg will swim upon the liquor, which is a sign that it is strong enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State observable, practical indicators (e.g., 'an egg will swim') used to judge when to proceed or stop a process, so readers understand decision criteria in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document apparatus and label components, include diagrams where useful
rubrics_metrics.description: See fig. 1, pl. 1; where A is the stream; B the fall of it; C the trunk into which it falls; L G a pipe; G the orifice of the pipe, or nose of the bellows; ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing mechanical arrangements, provide a labeled diagram and define each part in the text to make the working principle and construction clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report physiological or hazardous effects observed during work
rubrics_metrics.description: We saw there a man, who had not been in the mines for above half a year before, so full of mercury... and was so paralytic, that he could not, with both his hands, carry a glass half full of wine to his mouth without spilling it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and report any adverse health effects or safety hazards observed (e.g., mercury poisoning, suffocation by mine 'damp') as part of the observational account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include attestations or witness corroboration for extraordinary claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Captain Silas Taylor ... related the manner how they were killed in Virginia, which he afterwards was pleased to give in writing, attested by two credible persons in whose presence it was done
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For remarkable or anecdotal reports, provide witness attestations or other corroboration to increase credibility and allow readers to judge reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerate explicit research questions and lines of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: He shews ... 4. What are the ways proper to estimate the greater or less coldness of bodies; ... 5. Whether in cold, the diffusion from cold bodies be made more strongly downwards; ... 6. Whether that tradition be true, that if frozen apples or eggs be thawed near the fire, they will be thereby spoiled; ... 10. How strong the expansion of freezing water is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a numbered list of concrete questions or hypotheses to guide experimental design and to communicate the aims and scope of the inquiry to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note observational limitations and avoid pursuing unsupported speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: But, to state what grounds I had for these thoughts, I said ... But, seeing it appears not by history that a comet has been seen at those determinate distances of time ... I shall not pursue this speculation; but rather suggest ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly acknowledge limits of evidence (e.g., weather, historical gaps) and avoid extended speculation when not supported; present more modest alternative suggestions or defer conclusions.
